- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and prices are falling, model often over-anticipates recovery; reduce forecast by 1–4% to avoid overshoot.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overreacts and forecasts continued ascent; cap forecast at 10–15% above peak for 2–3 periods.  
- If sentiment is volatile or mixed (0.3–0.7), model exhibits mean-reversion bias — forecast should be adjusted toward historical 30-day average if deviation >2σ.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period rallies (last 5–7 days); add 0.5–1.5% to final 5–7 forecast points if sentiment turns positive.  
- If sentiment history shows rising optimism (e.g., 3+ consecutive increases), model tends to lag; add 0.5–2% to forecast for next 3–5 periods.  
- When sentiment is low and prices are near 30-day low, model often overcorrects upward — reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid false breakout.
